title_as_printed: Experimental Henry Coefficients for Nitrogen in Liquid Water at Various Temperatures

footnotes_as_printed.a: Delta is the percent deviation [see Eq. (16)] either from smoothing function Eq. (17) (CG) or Eq. (18) (BK). Average percent deviations [see Eq. (19)] are: <Delta>_CG = 0.038, and <Delta>_BK = 0.042.

pressure_note: P = total equilibrium pressure (water vapour + N2), determined by an iterative procedure (Ref. 6 of the paper) from the measurements; printed as 10^-3 P (Pa), i.e. kPa. Henry coefficient refers to the saturation pressure of water at T.

value.what: Henry coefficient H_2,1(T,Ps,1) = lim (f2/x2) at saturation pressure of water, fugacity-based (f2 = H x2 as x2->0), includes vapour-phase compressibility Z and fugacity coefficient phi_2 corrections and Poynting-corrected form H = h Z phi_2 / P_2, Eq. (12)

value2.what: 'uncorrected' Henry coefficient h_2,1 from measured amounts of N2 in vapour and liquid samples, Eq. (10)

extra_unmapped: Z phi_2 (vapour-phase compressibility times fugacity coefficient, calculated)
Delta_CG, Delta_BK (percent deviations from smoothing equations)
conversion_needs: pressure printed as 10^-3 P (Pa); Henry printed as 10^-9 H (Pa)
notes: Rows are individual experiments. Four rows at 298.14-298.16 K at different pressures (45.9 to 100.4 kPa) show pressure independence. Experimental H_2,1 is itself derived from measured moles of gas in each phase (value is the authors' processed Henry coefficient). Page is printed rotated 90 degrees.
